questions.subject: English Language and Comprehension
questions.questionText:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow by selecting the most appropriate option from the given alternatives.

In today's digital age, convenience often comes at the cost of privacy. Every time a user browses a website, clicks a link, or uses an app, their data is collected-sometimes without their knowledge. Companies use this information to target ads, predict behavior, or even sell insights to third parties. While this can lead to better services, it also raises ethical concerns. Who controls this data? How is it stored, and can users truly opt out? Many people accept terms and conditions without reading them, unknowingly giving permission for data tracking. Some countries have passed laws to protect user data, but implementation remains weak. As surveillance tools grow smarter, the line between public and private becomes blurred. Individuals must now learn to balance the benefits of technology with the right to privacy-a task that requires awareness, regulation, and responsible digital behavior.

What is the main concern raised in the passage?

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is gradually transforming the way students learn. From virtual tutors to personalized learning paths, AI helps identify each learner's strengths and weaknesses. With the help of data, AI systems can suggest specific topics where students need improvement. Schools are also using AI chatbots to answer basic queries, reducing the pressure on teachers. However, experts warn that over-dependence on AI may limit critical thinking. If students rely too much on machines for answers, they may lose problem-solving skills. There are also concerns about data privacy, especially when student performance data is stored online. Despite these issues, many educators believe AI can be a useful tool when used wisely.
